title: Three Months and One Short Stamp
subtitle: 国家公民 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 国家公民（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·国家与公民）
meta: 主题语境：国家公民（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·国家与公民）　|　核心词汇：rank　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 rank 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1964 the clerk ① earned the rank that no applicant in the office would have counted, and he said the earning was the whole of the month. The ② rank, meaning the grade itself and not the stamp, ran three months and stayed uncounted in the book; a rank, he said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ rank in that office had the same short stamp beside it, and the ④ rank at the far counter, meaning the form they kept for the children to sign and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A rank, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the clerk said the counting is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the rank was the whole of the matter, meaning the status and not the grade. The ⑥ rank, meaning the status and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; rank, he said, is either something you earn or the only word that means both a grade and a status. He said the status is the part they remember.

By 1969 the ⑦ rank had become a line in a file, and the file had become an argument about the short stamp. The ⑧ rank of the whole thing, the clerk wrote in May, was one office and three months of counting; rank, he said, is either the form at the far counter or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ rank I remember is the grade counted in the file, which closed in 1971 and is still counted as the quietest in the office. A ⑩ rank, my mother said in 1973, is the only grade that improves by being counted; every rank, she said, is a status that has agreed to look like a grade. She said the status was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 等级；军衔（指办事处里每一级旁边的那一级）
B. n. 等级；军衔（指那级等级本身，与小小的印章相对）
C. 固定搭配：earn the rank 挣得这一级等级
D. n. 等级；军衔（指留给孩子们签的那一份）
E. n. 等级之事（抽象总称，指一处办事处的等级之事）
F. n. 等级；军衔（指卷宗里写到、被清点的那一级）
G. n. 等级、名位（指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 名位（抽象总称，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: earned the rank that no applicant in the office would have counted
The rank, meaning the grade itself and not the stamp
the rank at the far counter
the rank was the whole of the matter
the rank had become a line in a file
The rank of the whole thing
A rank, my mother said in 1973

answers.why: earn the rank 意为“挣得这一级等级”，1964 年那位书记员把办事处里没有一位申请人肯清点的一级等级做了一遍。
rank 意为“等级；军衔”，指那级等级本身而不是小小的印章，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被清点。
rank 意为“等级；军衔”，指办事处里每一级旁边的那一级，每一级旁边都有同一枚小小的印章。
rank 意为“等级；军衔”，指最远那个窗口的留给孩子们签的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
rank 意为“等级、名位”，指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这级名位就是那件事的全部。
rank 意为“名位”，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西而不是那级等级，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
rank 意为“等级；军衔”，指卷宗里写到、被清点的那一级，到 1969 年这一级成了卷宗里的一行。
rank 意为“等级之事”，书记员五月写道，整件事的等级之事是一处办事处和三个月份的清点。
rank 意为“等级；军衔”，我记得的是卷宗里清点过的那一级，1971 年办结了，至今仍被说成办事处里最安静的一级。
rank 为抽象总称，母亲 1973 年说，等级是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的等级。
